I've been farming this 18 mu for 40 years, since I was 15. My husband and I are both 55 now, and our son works in Shijiazhuang, so it's mostly the two of us. I also pick up a few days a week at the garment factory in town when they're busy — that brings in some cash, but it means we're short on labor during the busy seasons.

The wheat went in last October around the 15th, same as always. I put down 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base — about 50 jin per mu, that's my rule of thumb. Now it's late April and the wheat is at jointing. I topdressed last week with about 20 kg of urea per mu. I wanted to do 25 kg because my neighbor Zhang did that and his wheat looks greener, but urea is 2.8 yuan per kg now and I have to save some money for the maize season. Still, I won't cut too much — two years ago I tried saving on fertilizer and the yield dropped to 380 kg per mu. That hurt. Better to waste a little money than risk a big loss.

For water, I'll irrigate twice more for wheat — once now at jointing, and once at heading in May if it doesn't rain. Each time costs about 15 yuan per mu for the pump electricity. Three times would be better but that's 45 yuan per mu just for water, and I need cash in hand for doctor visits or emergencies. Two times is what I can afford. For pests, I sprayed herbicide in March. If I see aphids or mildew later, I'll spray again, but I don't spray preventively — chemicals cost money and I'm not sure they're needed every year.

For the maize, after we harvest the wheat in early June — probably around June 10th — we have exactly one week to get the maize in the ground. I hire Old Wang's tractor for 35 yuan per mu. He comes the same day we harvest, plows quickly, and plants. I can't do 18 mu by hand in that heat at my age, and my husband's back isn't what it used to be. I buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed from the shop in town — about 2.5 kg per mu, costs around 40 yuan. It's reliable. I've used it for five years and it usually gives me 450–500 kg per mu. I don't save my own maize seed because hybrids don't breed true.

For maize fertilizer, I put 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at planting, same as wheat. Then at the big-flare stage in July, I topdress about 18 kg of urea per mu. The extension agent said I should do more — maybe 22 kg urea — but that's too much for my wallet. I do what I can afford. Irrigation for maize depends on the summer rains. I'll plan to irrigate once at tasseling, and maybe once more at grain filling if August is dry. But if it rains, I skip it and save the pump money. For maize pests, I always do one herbicide spray, and last year there were corn borers in the village, so I'll probably need insecticide too.

I expect about 430 kg per mu for wheat and 460 kg per mu for maize. I'm not trying to break records — I want steady, reliable yields. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, so I play it safe.
